description: StorageBackend cross-SDK conformance: pluggable storage primitive shared by ErrorHistory, UsageCollector, and MetricsCollector. Verifies the four-method contract (save, get, list, delete), namespace isolation, and idempotent delete (Issue #43, D-39).

test_cases.description: A value written via save() under a (namespace, key) tuple is returned verbatim by a subsequent get() call against the same tuple.
list() with a prefix returns only entries whose keys start with that prefix, in any order; without prefix it returns the full namespace.
delete() against an absent key is a no-op (no error). After deletion, subsequent get() returns null/None.
Entries written under namespace 'errors' MUST NOT be visible from namespace 'metrics'. The same key string under different namespaces denotes distinct records.
Calling save() on an existing (namespace, key) MUST overwrite the previous value; get() returns the most recent write.

D-113. §1.1 made the `StorageBackend` argument a MUST and never named the namespaces, so of NINE collector/SDK combinations only four wrote anything, and the two SDKs that wrote ErrorHistory records used different names (`errors` vs `error_history`). A namespace IS the key a caller queries by, so an unnamed one made the argument write-only — or, in five of nine, not even that.

The case drives all three bundled collectors through ONE backend and asserts the exact set of namespaces it received. A per-collector case would let an SDK that writes two of three pass two cases and fail one, which reads as a partial gap; the set assertion says plainly that the surface is three namespaces, not three independent behaviours.

D-113's other half: 'when omitted, `InMemoryStorageBackend` MUST be used'. Only apcore-typescript honoured it, so the SAME omission produced a working store there and a silent no-op elsewhere — and a caller reading records back got an empty list rather than an error, which is the shape that hides longest.

Asserted as READABILITY rather than as a type name: what the caller can observe is that a record written with no backend supplied is still there to read. A type-name assertion would also pin each SDK's spelling of the class, which is not what the decision says.

driver_contract.value_is_a_json_object: `value` is a JSON OBJECT, not a scalar and not opaque bytes: apcore-python types it `dict`, apcore-typescript `Record<string, unknown>`, apcore-rust `serde_json::Value` (structurally wider, same requirement). All three collectors — ErrorHistory, UsageCollector, MetricsCollector — store records. Drivers MUST use object values; a driver that passes a scalar is testing a shape no collector produces, and would have made the bytes-based Redis example in features/observability.md look conformant.
driver_contract.delete_is_idempotent: Deleting an absent key is a no-op that MUST NOT raise. Assert the second delete of the same key succeeds, not merely that the first one did.
driver_contract.namespace_isolation: Assert the negative direction too: a key written under namespace A MUST NOT be readable via namespace B, and MUST NOT appear in B's list().
